### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/your-first-project.mdx`  _(via sys_note (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line), sys_task (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b69f7157cdd263196f3b5587000f5963c9d27fe2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `366b7e8f790542e653c3f5d6ac24414c610a397c` — the merge of head `e7621c87692c7e7d51eca79af7c707bfa73b3013` into base `b69f7157cdd263196f3b5587000f5963c9d27fe2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 366b7e8f790542e653c3f5d6ac24414c610a397c && git checkout 366b7e8f790542e653c3f5d6ac24414c610a397c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b69f7157cdd263196f3b5587000f5963c9d27fe2 e7621c87692c7e7d51eca79af7c707bfa73b3013 && git checkout -B drift-repro b69f7157cdd263196f3b5587000f5963c9d27fe2 && git merge --no-ff e7621c87692c7e7d51eca79af7c707bfa73b3013

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b69f7157cdd263196f3b5587000f5963c9d27fe2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b69f7157cdd263196f3b5587000f5963c9d27fe2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e7621c87692c7e7d51eca79af7c707bfa73b3013`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/work/sys-task.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/work/sys-note.object.ts (the two docblocks that teach the entry the check judges). The new test file and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of `defineStack` / `os validate`: unchanged, and that is right. The hunk sits inside the existing `if (!nav.requiresObject)` arm of the app-navigation check in `validateCrossReferences`; the condition that reaches `errors.push` (`type === 'object'`, a string `objectName` absent from `objectNames`, no `requiresObject`) is untouched, and exactly one error is pushed on both sides of the new ternary. No input accepted on `main` is refused at this head, and none refused on `main` is accepted.
- Public surface: one refusal message changes, for names `isPlatformObjectName` matches (the `sys_` / `cloud_` / `ai_` prefix test, `hasPlatformObjectPrefix`). Its first sentence is the old message byte for byte, so a consumer matching on the prefix holds; a name without the prefix gets the old string whole. The only exact-match pin of this message in the tree (`stack-artifact-crossref.test.ts`, `crm_case`) names an unprefixed object and is unaffected. Envelope code (`STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID`) and status (422) are unchanged. Right.
- Both nav containers (`app.navigation`, `areas[].navigation`) and nested `children` go through the same `checkNavItems`, so the new message reaches every position the refusal does. Right.
- No schema key, no exported symbol, no generated baseline moves; `requiresObject` on `NavigationItem` is read, not changed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no. Confirmed from the tree: message text plus two docblocks, no accept-set or type change. The changeset declares `patch` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`, which matches what the diff publishes (a message string; docblock text carried in the declarations). `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness` concluded success on this head. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no protocol door is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Route flag (shape B over shape A of the card): answered, B holds. The prefix test cannot tell `sys_task` from a plugin object such as `sys_approval_request` or a cloud one such as `sys_app`, so a prefix exemption would admit a menu entry with no runtime hiding for an absent object. The neighbouring checks that do exempt the prefix (seed data, grants, child lists) have no client-side capability gate to fall back on; the navigation entry does, and `requiresObject` is that gate.
- `open_questions` entry (exempt the curated `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` group instead): answered, not taken here. Its premise is true (`sys_task` and `sys_note` are both in that group), but it is an accept-set widening owing its own Clause-② reading, and `packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts` shows the two work objects are registered through the manifest service inside a try that only warns on failure ("Applications that put them in their navigation will find no such object on this kernel"), so `requiresObject` keeps a runtime meaning even for these two. A separate card if the maintainer wants shorter starter entries; nothing is owed on this head.
- Deviation, local gate list narrowed to 20 commands and `check:i18n` not measured locally: answered by the check-runs on this head. Every completed run concluded success; the skipped ones are path-filtered or opt-in jobs (Lint UI, Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, the sharded Dogfood matrix placeholder, Temporal Conformance, the opt-in harnesses, the queue verdict pair). No failure, none pending.
- Deviation, commit trailer form: outside this record's face; no contract effect.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; `isPlatformObjectName` is a string prefix test on a name already in hand.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, against the card and its first consumers (`examples/app-starter/src/apps/starter.app.ts`, the platform catalog skill row for `sys_task`):

- The message tells the truth about the fix. `requiresObject` is tested for truthiness only, so the literal the message prints (`requiresObject: 'NAME'`) clears the refusal; the parenthesis "the menu then hides it wherever the object is not registered" agrees with the key's own describe in `ui/app.zod.ts` ("Hide/disable this entry unless the named object is registered in the runtime"). The starter app and the catalog row already write the entry this way, so the error, the docblocks, the skill and the example now teach one shape.
- "do not declare a copy of the object in this package" is consistent with the single-owner rule the registration comment in `plugin.ts` cites (a host declaring its own `sys_task` is refused), and with the reserved-prefix rule on a stack's own objects.
- The in-code comment states the reason the refusal stays, and the reason is what the code does. It does not contradict the `isPlatformObjectName` jsdoc ("cross-reference checks must not demand they appear in `config.objects`"): the entry is still not required to be declared, it is required to carry its gate.
- Attempt to break it, typo path: `sys_taks` now draws the hint and, once `requiresObject: 'sys_taks'` is added, passes `defineStack`. That was already true on `main` for anyone who knew the key, and `@objectstack/lint` `validate-object-references` checks both `requiresObject` and the gated `objectName` against the curated registry, so the fictional name still surfaces as an advisory. No new hole.
- Attempt to break it, unprefixed plugin object: unchanged behaviour and unchanged message; the hint is withheld where the stack's own typo is the likelier cause. Sound.

`packages/platform-objects/src/work/sys-task.object.ts` and `sys-note.object.ts`, sentence by sentence against the check:

- "The entry needs `requiresObject` — `defineStack` refuses a menu entry for an object the stack does not declare unless the entry says the object comes from elsewhere": agrees with the arm reviewed above.
- `sys_note`, "Every environment carries it": agrees with `plugin.ts`, which registers `SysTask` and `SysNote` together in one manifest; the sentence is as true for the note as the existing one is for the task.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (accepted deviations, no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — the message asserts "is provided by the platform or a plugin" on the prefix test alone, so a mistyped `sys_` name is told the same. "expected from the platform or a plugin" would be exact; the lint advisory covers the case.
- N2 (nit) — the docblock entry `{ type: 'object', objectName: 'sys_task', requiresObject: 'sys_task' }` omits the `id` every navigation item requires. It reads as a fragment showing the keys that matter, and the starter app and the catalog row show the full entry.
